I found comprehensive information about browser storage options for state persistence. Here's a summary of the search results:

## Browser Storage Options for State Persistence (2026)

The search results cover the main browser storage mechanisms suitable for persisting application state:

### localStorage
localStorage is the most widely known browser storage API that provides a simple way to store persistent key–value data inside the browser. This makes localStorage ideal for storing small pieces of persistent application state. However, the synchronous nature means localStorage operations block the main thread, which is why it should only be used for small data.

### IndexedDB
When developers need to store large amounts of structured data, IndexedDB becomes the primary solution. IndexedDB is best for applications with large, complex, or structured state data (e.g., offline-first apps, apps handling large media files). IndexedDB handles large data efficiently unlike localStorage or SessionStorage (which have a size limit of around 5MB), IndexedDB is a low-level API that allows storage of much larger amounts of data.

### Hybrid Approaches
Recent 2026 articles discuss combining storage methods for optimal performance. The golden rule: localStorage for preferences, IndexedDB for everything else. For complex applications requiring SQL capabilities, the sql.js + IndexedDB combination is currently the most compatible way to get persistent SQL in the browser.

## Tool Call Streaming & Real-Time Rendering

The tool-call pattern dictates that the state of the tool's execution must be streamed and rendered in the UI in real-time, creating a transparent, trustworthy user experience. The UI progresses through distinct states: Initiation where the AI decides to call a tool and the UI renders a placeholder like a loading spinner, Execution where the streaming connection keeps the UI element active while the server-side function runs, and Completion where the loading state is replaced by actual content rendered as a distinct component.

## Smooth Streaming Animations

A pattern called smooth text streaming addresses how most AI apps show text appearing in chunks as it arrives from the server, which can create a jarring user experience where text appears in bursts instead of flowing naturally. Decoupling network streaming from visual streaming works by receiving chunks from the server, buffering them, and displaying them character-by-character at a consistent speed.

## Standardized Event Protocols

AG-UI adds a protocol layer between the agent and the UI that standardizes interactions, streaming structured events that the UI can react to in real time instead of one-off responses. The protocol includes event types like TEXT_MESSAGE_START, TOOL_CALL_START (with metadata like toolCallId), TOOL_CALL_ARGS (enabling live rendering of parameter inputs), and TOOL_CALL_END (including the result payload).

## Event-Based Architecture Benefits

AG-UI employs an event-based architecture where agents stream updates while working, allowing interfaces to show progress in real-time whether the agent is generating text, calling tools, or updating shared state. Treating agent interactions as an event log rather than mutable state, modeling user inputs, LLM chunks, tool calls, and UI actions as a single event stream lets you project state for the UI without drift.

## Key Security Patterns

When calling AI SDK functions directly, API keys would be exposed on the client, so calls need to be proxied via a server SDK which adds the API keys to the calls.

AI SDK Core handles server-side AI operations with functions like generateText and streamText, while AI SDK UI provides client-side hooks for building interactive interfaces, including useChat and useCompletion.

## Browser API Key Security Concerns

Regarding client-side storage, if secrets are handled in the browser, a malicious extension can easily scrape them, which is a client-side vulnerability.

## Encryption Approaches for Sensitive Data

For applications requiring encryption patterns, Cloud KMS (using AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, or Azure Key Vault) is considered best practice, where your application is granted IAM permissions to use a key for encryption/decryption, but it never actually holds the key material itself.

## Transport and Extensibility

The new useChat hook has flexible transports that can swap out the default fetch-based transport for custom implementations, allowing WebSockets for real-time communication or direct connections to LLM providers without a backend for client-only applications.

The general recommendation is to keep API keys on the server side and use the Vercel AI SDK's UI hooks on the client to communicate with your backend, rather than attempting to store or encrypt keys in the browser.

# Multi-Agent Dashboard Research Report — brocco.ai/app

## 1. Pixel-by-pixel patterns from real 2026 multi-agent tools

**Google Antigravity (Gemini 3, Nov 2025 launch, April 2026 update).** Two surfaces. The **Editor View** is a VS Code shell with a center editor pane, an **Agent Side Panel** on the right, and an **Artifacts Panel** holding task lists, plans, diffs, screenshots, and browser recordings. The **Manager Surface** is the multi-agent supervisor — after the April 2026 overhaul it's a **three-column layout**: left = walkthrough/agent index, center = preview, right = details. Agents are spawned from the Manager and communicate through Artifacts rather than raw logs ([Google blog](https://developers.googleblog.com/build-with-google-antigravity-our-new-agentic-development-platform/), [April update](https://antigravitylab.net/en/articles/antigravity/antigravity-features-update-april-2026)).

**Cursor 3 "Glass" (April 2, 2026).** Killed the Composer side-pane. Replaced with an **Agents Window**: a unified sidebar listing all agents — local, Cloud (formerly Background), and ones kicked off from mobile/Slack/GitHub/Linear — in one place. **Up to 8 agents in parallel on a single prompt.** Each agent runs in an isolated git-worktree copy of the codebase. Plan-then-build is explicit: pick a plan model, pick a build model, optionally fan out to multiple parallel plans for review ([Cursor 2.0 changelog](https://cursor.com/changelog/2-0), [Cursor 3 InfoQ](https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/04/cursor-3-agent-first-interface/)).

**Devin (Cognition).** Workspace = **4 tabbed views**: Shell, Browser, Editor (with diff + "Global Work View" of all modified files), and Planner. Every command/edit/click is recorded into a **timelapse replay**. For multiple Devins, the dashboard is a list of sessions with status pills ([Devin docs](https://docs.devin.ai/work-with-devin/devin-session-tools)).

**Windsurf 2.0 Agent Command Center.** A **Kanban board inside the IDE**: columns are In Progress / Blocked / Ready for Review. Each card is an agent. Best example of "supervisor view" today ([Windsurf 2.0](https://www.productcool.com/product/windsurf-2-0)).

**Replit Agent 4 (March 11, 2026).** **Design Canvas** is an infinite zoomable board where multiple agents (auth, DB, frontend, backend) run simultaneously, work moves through draft → active → review states, and a **conflict-resolver sub-agent** auto-merges when two agents touch the same files ([Replit blog](https://blog.replit.com/introducing-agent-4-built-for-creativity), [agent4 page](https://replit.com/agent4)).

**Claude Code multi-agent.** Terminal-native. Multiple spinners stack vertically, each with the 3-5-word agent description. Power users layer **tmux split panes** so each subagent gets its own visible window. Open-source "Claude Agent Teams UI" wraps this in Electron + React with a Kanban + diff viewer ([MindStudio guide](https://www.mindstudio.ai/blog/claude-code-agent-teams-parallel-workflows)).

**Codex CLI (OpenAI).** Full-screen TUI. Recent additions: **persisted /goal workflows** with create/pause/resume/clear, plan-mode nudges, action-required terminal titles, configurable status line, `@` fuzzy file picker in the composer ([Codex changelog](https://developers.openai.com/codex/changelog)).

**Amp by Sourcegraph.** Thread-style conversation as the primary surface. Subagents spawned via the Task tool, each with isolated context. New **Thread Map** view visualizes how parallel threads connect — closest thing to a "supervisor graph" shipping today ([Thread Map](https://hackernoon.com/sourcegraph-spinoff-amp-rolls-out-thread-map-to-manage-agent-workflows), [Amp manual](https://ampcode.com/manual)).

**GitHub Copilot Workspace.** Plan → Spec → Implement flow. Every tool invocation surfaced inline with approve/reject. Strong **"Undo Last Edit"** control in the view title bar — a pattern worth stealing ([Copilot Workspace](https://githubnext.com/projects/copilot-workspace/)).

**VS Code multi-agent (Feb 2026).** Native multi-agent panel — multiple agents in one window, each as a collapsible card with status badge, current tool call, and a "view diff" button ([VS Code blog](https://code.visualstudio.com/blogs/2026/02/05/multi-agent-development)).

## 2. Killer interactions worth copying

- **Tool-call render pattern (3-state)**: Initiation placeholder → Execution streaming → Completion swap-in of structured component (table, diff, screenshot). Makes every tool call feel like a live atom, not a log line ([patterns.dev](https://www.patterns.dev/react/ai-ui-patterns/), [Stackademic](https://stackademic.com/blog/the-tool-call-render-pattern-turning-your-ai-from-a-chatty-bot-into-a-doer)).
- **Smooth streaming** — buffer chunks, paint character-by-character at constant rate. Prevents jarring bursts ([Upstash](https://upstash.com/blog/smooth-streaming)).
- **AG-UI event protocol** — TEXT_MESSAGE_START, TOOL_CALL_START/ARGS/END events. Lets the UI render args **as they arrive** (e.g., a function call literally types its arguments live) ([AG-UI](https://docs.ag-ui.com/introduction)).
- **Plan-then-fan-out animation** — Cursor 3 shows the plan, then visibly spawns N agent cards from the plan. Steal the spawn animation.
- **Replay timelapse** (Devin) — scrub bar over the entire session.
- **Artifact-not-log surfacing** (Antigravity) — agents emit deliverables, not logs.
- **Agent nicknames + cleaner picker UI** (Codex 2026) — small thing, huge readability win.
- **Send-to-all / broadcast prompt** — single composer, checkbox row of "which agents receive this?", multi-target send. The fan-out pattern from ADK.
- **Drag-to-spawn / drag-to-merge** — Replit Canvas. Drag a card off the board = spawn; drag two together = merge.

## 3. BYOK patterns in 2026

The standard 2026 pattern is **client-side-only key storage with very loud trust copy**. Examples:

- **JetBrains AI Assistant**: Settings panel field, key stored in the OS secure credential store, never round-trips to JetBrains servers ([JetBrains BYOK](https://www.jetbrains.com/help/ai-assistant/bring-your-own-key-byok.html)).
- **GitHub Copilot BYOK** (Jan 2026): supports AWS Bedrock, Google AI Studio, OpenAI-compatible endpoints; key entered in Copilot settings ([GitHub changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-01-15-github-copilot-bring-your-own-key-byok-enhancements/)).
- **Factory CLI**: keys live in `~/.factory/settings.json` with explicit copy "**Your API keys remain local and are not uploaded to Factory servers**", supports `${ENV_VAR}` interpolation ([Factory docs](https://docs.factory.ai/cli/byok/overview)).
- **BYOKList directory** trust copy patterns: "Zero servers, zero accounts, zero cost" / "No backend, no accounts, no tracking" / "Zero AI markup — pay providers directly" ([byoklist.com](https://byoklist.com/)).
- **Warp**: dedicated "Bring Your Own API Key" settings page, model picker tied to the key ([Warp docs](https://docs.warp.dev/support-and-community/plans-and-billing/bring-your-own-api-key/)).

**Trust UI vocabulary that works in 2026**: green padlock badge next to the key field, tooltip "Stored in your browser only. Never sent to brocco.ai servers.", a "Test key" button that pings the provider directly from the browser, and a session-token model where the key encrypts a derived token rather than living in plaintext.

## 4. State persistence patterns

The 2026 consensus for browser dashboards is **hybrid: localStorage for prefs, IndexedDB for everything else** ([BSWEN guide](https://docs.bswen.com/blog/2026-04-07-localstorage-vs-sessionstorage-indexeddb/), [Medium guide](https://medium.com/@dulthiwanka2015/the-ultimate-guide-to-browser-storage-localstorage-indexeddb-cookies-and-more-98cab135d79a)).

Modern stack:
- **localStorage** (5 MB cap, sync) — theme, layout prefs, last-active agent, BYOK key (encrypted with WebCrypto-derived key from a passphrase or session key).
- **IndexedDB** via **Dexie.js** or **idb-keyval** — agent specs, run history, transcripts, artifacts, tool-call logs. Unlimited-ish, async, indexed.
- **OPFS (Origin Private File System)** — large binary artifacts (screenshots, model outputs, recorded browser sessions).
- **Optional server sync** — Supabase / Cloudflare D1 / Convex for cross-device. Local is canonical, server is the cache. Use **CRDT** (Yjs or Automerge) if real-time multi-tab matters.
- **Zustand + persist middleware** is the dominant React state shape; pair with `idb-keyval` storage adapter.
- For SQL-like queries over history: **sql.js + IndexedDB** is the 2026 standard ([recca0120](https://recca0120.github.io/en/2026/03/06/browser-storage-comparison/)).

## 5. Opinionated recommendation for brocco.ai/app

**The layout is a 3-row × 3-column desktop chrome with a configurable agent pane grid in the center, anchored by a single command bar.** Steal Antigravity's Manager-surface confidence, Cursor's parallel agent sidebar, Replit's Canvas spirit, Devin's tabbed-per-agent depth, and AG-UI's streaming protocol.

```css
.app {
  display: grid;
  height: 100vh;
  grid-template-columns: 240px 1fr 320px;
  grid-template-rows: 48px 1fr 88px;
  grid-template-areas:
    "header  header  header"
    "library panes   inspector"
    "library prompt  inspector";
  background: #0b0b0f;
  color: #e7e7ea;
}
.header    { grid-area: header; }
.library   { grid-area: library; }   /* Agent Library + Saved Specs */
.panes     { grid-area: panes;       /* Live agent grid (CSS subgrid) */
             display: grid;
             gap: 8px;
             grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(380px, 1fr));
             grid-auto-rows: minmax(280px, 1fr);
             padding: 8px;
             overflow: auto; }
.prompt    { grid-area: prompt; }    /* Single broadcast composer */
.inspector { grid-area: inspector; } /* Selected-agent deep view */
```

**Header (48px)** — left: brocco wordmark + workspace switcher. Center: BYOK status pill (green padlock, "Anthropic key · stored in browser", click → modal). Right: model picker, "Run all", "Stop all", avatar. Lift the **Undo Last Edit** control from Copilot Workspace.

**Library (240px, left rail)** — collapsible. Tabs: **Agents** (saved specs you can drag onto the canvas), **Plans** (multi-step recipes), **History** (yesterday's sessions, replayable). Bottom: "New Agent" CTA. Drag a Library card onto the pane grid = spawn. This is the "drag-to-spawn" moment.

**Panes (center)** — auto-fill grid of agent cards, each card is a **mini Devin** (4 tabs: Stream, Tools, Files, Browser). Card header: nickname + colored status dot (idle/thinking/tool-call/blocked/done) + "send to all" checkbox + close. Stream tab uses the AG-UI tool-call render pattern: live arg-typing animation, then result component swap-in, smooth-streamed text. Cards resize via CSS Grid; drag two cards onto each other = "merge plans" interaction.

**Prompt bar (88px, bottom, full-width)** — Antigravity-style. Single textarea with `@` fuzzy mention to target a specific agent or plan, model picker on the left, **Broadcast** chip on the right (when on, message fans out to every selected card with a visible spawn animation: text leaves the bar and splits into N copies that fly to each card). `Cmd+Enter` sends. Below the textarea: thin row of attached files / context.

**Inspector (320px, right rail)** — when a card is selected: full transcript, tool-call timeline (scrubbable replay), diff viewer, raw JSON of last response, "Fork this agent" button. When nothing selected: workspace-wide **Thread Map** (Amp-style graph of how agents relate) + cost meter (tokens spent, tied to the BYOK key).

**Persistence**: Zustand + idb-keyval. Agent specs and run history in IndexedDB; theme/layout/BYOK-encrypted-key in localStorage; large artifacts in OPFS. WebCrypto-derive an encryption key from a session passphrase so the BYOK key is never plaintext at rest. Wire optional Supabase sync behind a "Sync to cloud" toggle — local-first, server-as-cache.

**Killer "wow" moments to ship day-one**: (1) plan-then-fan-out animation from prompt bar to N cards, (2) live tool-call args typing themselves, (3) drag-to-spawn from Library, (4) `Cmd+K` palette to broadcast to checked cards, (5) Inspector replay scrubber.

This layout reads as Antigravity's Manager Surface fused with Cursor 3's Agents Window, with Replit's Canvas energy in the center grid and Devin's depth in each card. It's defensible, denser than competitors at the same width, and BYOK-trust is loud in the chrome.
